newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank to reject VSZ request.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank to reject VSZ request.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Tuesday it will reject a request by steel maker VSZ a.s. to increase its holdings in bank IRB a.s. to over 20 percent.
"We will reject the VSZ (issue) on Wednesday," Tibor Kasiak, head of the NBS banking supervision board, told Reuters, declining further comment.

He did not make it clear whether the rejection would also affect VSZ's current holdings in IRB, which caused a stir when it was recently revealed that VSZ might have exceeded the upper limit of 15 percent.
In August, VSZ asked for central bank permission to increase its stake in IRB, the third largest Slovak commercial bank, to over 20 percent.

Shortly after the request was filed, the Central Securities Registry (SCP) published figures showing VSZ already held some 20 percent of IRB, but later retracted the figures without further explanation.
According to Slovak law, any acquisition of over 15 percent stake in a commercial bank has to be approved by the NBS.

Kasiak said recently the NBS had still not received an official SCP statement on VSZ's current holdings in IRB, but would reverse the entire acquisition if it was found that VSZ's current holdings in the bank exceed the limit.
He did not say whether the NBS has now received the information from the SCP.
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
